title: Flower Garden
body:
Goal: use parameters so one function draws many different flowers, and a function that returns the turning angle.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. All three flowers land on top of each other and have the wrong number of petals.
  2. TODO 1: petal_turn() should return 360 / petals.
  3. TODO 2 and 3: use t.goto(x, y) so each flower appears where it was asked to.
  4. TODO 4: repeat once for each petal: range(petals).

Done looks like: three flowers side by side: 5, 8 and 12 petals, each with a green stem and a yellow middle.

Extra: add more flowers with different sizes. Can you make a whole row with a for loop? Try for x in range(-200, 201, 100):

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run it and look at the picture. The flowers sit in one spot and all have the same number of petals. Find the places in draw_flower and petal_turn that use fixed numbers instead of the values you are given.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: A full turn is 360 degrees, and the petals share it equally. Use division with /. The turtle can jump with t.goto(x, y). A for loop with range() repeats a set number of times, and that number can be a parameter.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Use return 360 / ____. In draw_flower, t.goto(____, ____) needs the parameters x and y. You need it before the stem, and the second goto should use it too. Change range(4) so it reads range(____), using the petal count.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Flower Garden
# draw_flower() should draw a flower anywhere, with any number of petals.
# Right now every flower lands in the same spot and has 4 petals. Fix it!

import turtle

PURPLE = "#CC79A7"
SKY = "#56B4E9"
ORANGE = "#E69F00"
YELLOW = "#F0E442"
GREEN = "#009E73"


def petal_turn(petals):
    """Return how many degrees to turn between petals so they go all the way round."""
    # TODO 1: a full turn is 360 degrees. Share it out between the petals.
    return 90


def draw_petal(t, size):
    """Draw one filled, leaf-shaped petal and end where it started."""
    t.begin_fill()
    t.circle(size, 60)
    t.left(120)
    t.circle(size, 60)
    t.left(120)
    t.end_fill()


def draw_flower(t, x, y, petals, color, size=60):
    """Draw a flower with its center at (x, y)."""
    t.penup()
    # TODO 2: go to (x, y) here, before drawing the stem.
    t.setheading(270)            # face down to draw the stem
    t.pendown()
    t.color(GREEN)
    t.pensize(4)
    t.forward(size * 1.5)
    t.penup()
    t.goto(0, 0)                 # TODO 3: back to the center: (x, y), not (0, 0)
    t.pendown()
    t.pensize(1)
    t.color("black", color)
    # TODO 4: repeat for the number of petals, not always 4.
    for _ in range(4):
        draw_petal(t, size)
        t.left(petal_turn(petals))
    t.dot(size // 3, YELLOW)     # the middle of the flower


if __name__ == "__main__":
    t = turtle.Turtle()
    t.speed(0)
    t.hideturtle()
    draw_flower(t, -180, 40, 5, PURPLE)
    draw_flower(t, 0, 80, 8, SKY, 70)
    draw_flower(t, 180, 20, 12, ORANGE, 50)
    turtle.done()
